text:
Anna Li: Hey team — customer Jensen (Acme) opened a ticket saying a bunch of their streaming responses are being marked as 5xx and billed. They see `broken pipe` in our logs but their client reports a clean close. Can we triage? :wave:
Jensen (Acme): yes — we kicked off a long streaming inference and midway the stream stopped. client shows HTTP/1.1 200 until our socket closed. We then got billed.
Anna Li: do you have the exact time and a request id?
Jensen (Acme): sure, request id `req-7f3c9b`, started ~2026-03-02T15:17:03Z. client logs: 
```
> recv returned 0 (EOF)
> connection closed by remote
> no error payload from server
```
They say they didn't see any error in body.
Mike Chen: tagging to oncall. my initial thought: gateway or our proxy is detecting a write to a closed socket and surfacing `EPIPE` -> we currently classify some EPIPE cases as 5xx if write fails after server side wrote an error. Need to confirm sequence.
Tess Alvarez: from billing POV, if it was a client-side disconnect we should not charge for the unconsumed tokens. if server returned 2xx then charged; if server aborted with 5xx then it's refundable. we need clear labeling.
Anna Li: I pulled gateway logs around req-7f3c9b. snippet: 
```
[2026-03-02T15:17:03Z] req-7f3c9b stream-start upstream=runtime-21
[2026-03-02T15:22:58Z] req-7f3c9b write-chunk size=512 status=200
[2026-03-02T15:23:05Z] req-7f3c9b write-error: EPIPE while writing chunk 45
[2026-03-02T15:23:05Z] req-7f3c9b proxy-status: 502 upstream-reset
```
So logs show write-error followed by proxy marking it as 502.
Jensen (Acme): client TCP shows a FIN at 15:23:04 and an ACK. we didn't send a FIN. question: is it plausible keepalive probes or intermediate proxy caused client appear to have closed?
Mike Chen: possible. We have a public gateway + internal runtime + edge CDN. Several places can emit keepalive probes or timeouts. Do you have full tcpdump?
Jensen (Acme): attaching a small pcap excerpt in the ticket — but TL;DR: client initiated FIN, we see server attempts to write after FIN and kernel returns EPIPE.
Anna Li: So client FIN first -> server writes -> EPIPE. That's a client disconnect case and should be classified as client-abort not 5xx. Why did the proxy return 502?
Mike Chen: our gateway has a heuristic: if the runtime fails with a non-2xx before we've flagged a client-close, we bubble up a 5xx. The client-close detection is based on read-side events from the TCP stack; with intermediate NATs/CDNs we sometimes observe FIN only at the edge after a delayed period. There are two failure modes: (1) client FIN -> we see it -> mark client-abort; (2) we observe write error while we haven't yet observed FIN -> classify 5xx. we need to make heuristics more tolerant.
Tess Alvarez: For billing the conservative route is to rollback charges for this request while we investigate. we can do a credit.
infra-bot: deploy 2026.03.02-21:11 rolled to gateway v3.14.2 (sha: a5c8f3) :rocket:
Mike Chen: Proposed short-term mitigations: 
- treat EPIPE during streaming as client-abort if we've seen any prior client data or if runtime had active read-socket errors within last 2s.
- if write error occurs, check TCP FIN timestamps from edge logs before deciding classification.
- expose raw tcp flags in gateway logs for ambiguous cases for billing review.
Long-term: update our metrics pipeline so billing uses the final classification produced by runtime after reap sequence, not intermediate proxy status.
Anna Li: can you share the minimal repro curl so we can reproduce locally? Jensen offered to help.
Jensen (Acme): here's a repro we used (node + curl interop): 
```
# server: simulate streaming and long payload
while true; do printf "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\nContent-Type: text/plain\r\n\r\n"; for i in {1..1000}; do printf "%x\r\nhello-world-\n\r\n" 11; sleep 0.5; done; done | nc -l 8080

# client: connect and close mid-stream
curl --no-buffer http://localhost:8080/ -o /dev/null &
# after 10s, simulate client close
sleep 10; pkill -f "curl --no-buffer"
```
This reproduces write-after-close.
Mike Chen: thanks. I reproduced locally with `socat` + tcpdump. Observed exactly `EPIPE` on write and our gateway returned 502. patch idea: when write fails with EPIPE during chunked transfer, check last-seen on client read side. if client FIN timestamp <= write timestamp -> mark client-abort and return nothing (i.e., no 5xx).
Tess Alvarez: once you have logs showing classification change, we'll reconcile billing. For now I've issued a temporary credit for request id `req-7f3c9b`.
Anna Li: can you post a short PR description for the gateway tweak and we can prioritize? also need a monitoring alert for sudden spikes in write_EPIPE->5xx conversions.
Mike Chen: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/gateway/pulls/842 - summary: "treat EPIPE during streaming as client disconnect if edge-FIN present within 3s; log edge-tcp-flags; add metric gateway.epipe.client_vs_server (labels: runtime_id, route)". added unit tests + integration test with simulated FIN race.
Jensen (Acme): thanks — can you also add an explicit header we can check in responses so our SDK can avoid reporting an error to users if server side actually considered it a client-abort? some header like `X-Redwood-Stream-Status: client-abort`?
Anna Li: good idea. will discuss with Mike. If we add a header we need to ensure we don't leak internal states. maybe header only for customers who opt-in via account flag.
Mike Chen: ack. I'll add a debug header under account opt-in and add docs.
Tess Alvarez: billing note: please tag any similar request ids in the last 24h to review for credits. I've created a billing queue ticket BQ-759.
Anna Li: next steps: (1) Prod hotfix to classification logic (Mike) (2) run backfill on the last 48h for EPIPE->5xx patterns and enqueue credits (Tess) (3) update support playbook + sample repro (Anna) (4) follow up with Jensen on header opt-in (Anna)
Jensen (Acme): appreciated — we'll monitor and share any more pcaps if we see repeats. thanks for quick handling :clap:
infra-bot: alert: gateway.epipe.client_vs_server spike detected 2026-03-03T02:01:12Z - rolling job requested.
Mike Chen: deploying patch to canary now. will report results in ~30m.
Anna Li: Thanks all — updating ticket and will close thread when patch is validated.
